title: Half of Australians Feel Overqualified for Their Jobs
paragraphs: Having qualifications and skills can help you find a job. But what if the job you end up in doesn't really require them?
That seems to be the case for many workers in Australia, with half saying they have more education than their job requires.

The finding comes from the latest Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia (HILDA) Survey, based on data collected in 2024. HILDA has surveyed Australians since 2001, with more than 17,000 people taking part each year.
The survey found that 49.5% of workers aged 18 to 64 believed they were overeducated for their job. One in four also felt overskilled, meaning their job did not make full use of their abilities.

The feeling is especially common among younger workers. Among 18- to 24-year-olds, 54% felt overeducated and 36% felt overskilled. The researchers say this may partly be because young people often work casual jobs while studying. And after finishing studies, they may take entry-level jobs that do not closely match their qualifications.
But feeling overqualified may have effects beyond simply being bored at work.

Workers who felt overeducated were less satisfied with their jobs and were more likely to think about quitting. They were also less satisfied with life in general. The effects were even stronger among people who felt overskilled.

The researchers said it's important that young people have the necessary support to move into jobs that match their education and skills as closely as possible. Workers should also be given more opportunities to keep learning, so that they can build new skills as jobs and workplaces change.
So, having more education and skills may sound like a good thing, but if you don't get to use them, it may not feel like much of an advantage.
